title: Autocalibrate burst damping — prototype notes and experiment plan
content:
Goal:
Short: reduce repeated short-lived burst coalescence in dedicated GPU pools that causes transient 10–30% tail-latency spikes and eviction cascades.

Why this doc exists:
- Captures on-call observations from the 2024-11-06 night surge (SRE rotation).
- Hypotheses for root causes that were not settled in earlier triage notes.
- Concrete, small experiments to try in a staging pool and how to measure success.

Observed symptoms (oncall notes):
- 23:07 UTC: multiple tenants experienced 99th p50-to-p99 latency inflation for small text-generation jobs (~16–64 tokens).
- 23:12 UTC: autoscaler triggered 1 additional pod per pooled-gpu node group, but cooldown kept other scale-ups suppressed causing backlog coalescence.
- 23:14 UTC: eviction alerts on 2 nodes; tenants A and C evicted (heavy batching workloads detected).
- 23:20 UTC: KV cache hit-rate dropped from 0.82 to 0.45 for the affected tenants; subsequent requests showed token re-generation overhead.
- 23:36 UTC: tail latency normalized after manual bump of burst-capacity to +20%.

Key telemetry snippets (promql-style, for reproducibility):
- avg_over_time(request_duration_seconds[5m]) by (pool)
- increase(allocator.evictions_total[15m])
- sum(rate(gpu_utilization_percent[1m])) by (node_pool)
- kvcache_hits_total / kvcache_requests_total by (tenant)
- autoscaler_scale_events_total{reason=~"burst|policy"}

Preliminary hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler hysteresis + short bursts: the autoscaler cooldown (default 10m) prevents compensating scale-ups for repeated short bursts from multiple tenants; result: backlog grows and the system opens eviction loops.
2) KV-cache amplification: cache invalidation for evicted tenants causes downstream re-generation of prefixes that then amplify GPU time per request.
3) Noisy affinity tenant: a tenant with aggressive continuous batching runs is briefly stealing cycles via affinity and causes other tenants to enter slower execution paths leading to queueing.
4) Scheduling packing thresholds too aggressive: we are overpacking smaller jobs onto fractional GPU slots; under contention, context-switch overhead jumps.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident (notes):
- Manual +20% burst-capacity allocation to affected regional pool (Mitigation A).
- Temporary per-tenant request-concurrency cap lowered from 8 -> 5 for suspected noisy tenant.
- Forced garbage-collection of a few stale KV cache shards for tenant C (we used cache-ctl flush --shard).
- Opened JIRA-4567 for follow-ups and metric gaps.

Experiment plan (staging pool, 48h each change, success metrics: p99 latency down 30% during synthetic coalesced bursts):
A) Reduce autoscaler cooldown from 10m -> 90s (staging only), keep scale-in cooldown unchanged. Rationale: respond quickly to repeated short bursts. Risks: thrash/extra infra churn, higher tail cost.
   - Measure: scale_events_total per hour, average time-to-scale (seconds), p95/p99 job latency, allocated GPUs/avg.

B) Introduce burst-damping layer: simple moving-window counter that suppresses scale-downs for N events and aggregates small burst requests into short-lived micro-batches before routing to GPU. Implementation notes: prototype in allocator service as feature-flag.
   - Measure: token throughput, batching size distribution, request latency distribution.

C) Tenant-level isolation tweak: if tenant uses batching > X qps and has >Y concurrent long-lived sessions, put on dedicated affinity lane with stricter preemption limits.
   - Measure: eviction frequency for co-located tenants, tail latency.

D) KV cache stability experiment: increase TTL for prefix-KV entries from 5m -> 15m for staging; observe hit-rate and memory pressure.
   - Measure: kvcache_hit_rate, redis/memcached eviction rates, gpu-work-per-request.

Operational runbook draft (quick steps for oncall to break feedback loops):
1) Identify if eviction cascade is active: check increase(allocator.evictions_total[5m]) > threshold (10).
2) If cascade: temporarily increase burst-capacity +15% for region (console -> capacity -> burst).
3) Throttle suspected noisy tenant: set concurrency-cap at tenant-level. Steps: api-admin tenants update --id <tenant> --concurrency 5.
4) If KV cache hit-rate < 0.6 for affected tenants, run cache-ctl flush --shard=affected_shards and monitor 5m windows. Note: flushing will cause regen overhead; only use after throttling.
5) If autoscaler shows no scale-up events while queueing grows, consider manual scale-up of node-pool (gcloud/terraform patch) and file an action-item to evaluate cooldown.
6) Follow up: create timeline entries in JIRA, tag oncall rotation, assign to eng-sre and allocator owners.

Measurement dashboards to create (first pass):
- Dedicated-pool: p50/p95/p99 latency by tenant and pool (5m rollup).
- Autoscaler events heatmap (by region, time-of-day).
- KV cache hit-rate and regeneration rate by tenant.
- Eviction cascade detector: derivative(evictions_total) with alert if > 5 spikes in 10m.

Open questions / unknowns (for investigation):
- Are the short bursts coming from a small set of tenants (repeat offenders) or many tenants simultaneously? We only sampled a few. Need to run forensic on request ids.
- Is there a specific model size or seq-len distribution correlated with the events? Get per-model breakdown.
- Do node-level processes (driver overhead/firmware anomalies) co-occur with the bursts? Check node exporter errors.

Notes-to-self / messy ideas (keep here for iteration):
- Could try a soft rate-limit token-bucket per-tenant that allows short spikes but delays immediate retries to avoid immediate coalescence.
- Maybe a queueing discipline change: prefer shallow queue preemption of oldest requests from suspect tenants.
- Explore ML classifier to detect noisy tenant signature (batch-size, qps, kvcache-miss pattern).

Next actionable owners and timeline:
- Marcus (eng-sre): set up staging experiments A/B for cooldown and burst-damping (start 2024-11-11).
- Elena (allocator): prototype burst-damping feature-flag in allocator service; small perf test.
- Samir (applied-ml): produce per-model sequence-length correlation report (due 2024-11-15).
- Aisha (owner): consolidate dashboards and push alert to pager duty channel.

Appendix: useful commands and queries
- Check eviction spikes: kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Evicted -A --since=15m
- Inspect autoscaler history: curl -sS http://allocator.internal/metrics | jq '.scale_events | .[-50:]'
- Quick KV cache hit rate per tenant (redis): HGETALL kv:tenant:<tenant-id>:stats

Slack threads and references:
- #sre-dedicated-capacity thread (link in linked_artifacts).
- Incident notes: JIRA-4567. PR for temporary throttle: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tenant-controls/pull/89

If this doc helps, we can convert to an oncall runbook and a short playbook page in Confluence. For now leaving as prototype notes — please drop comments inline or ping in #sre-dedicated-capacity.

— Aisha
